items.title: Coachella Reveals 2027 Lineup
items.summary:
Coachella released its 2027 lineup, confirming months of speculation about the top of the bill: Dua Lipa, Tame Impala and SZA will headline the festival's return to the Empire Polo Club in Indio. The event runs across two weekends, April 9-11 and April 16-18, following its usual format.

Daddy Yankee occupies the slot at the bottom of the poster that Coachella typically reserves for a quasi-headliner, a position that carries roughly the same weight as the three names above it. Madonna is billed in the dance tent. The Bunker, which housed a Radiohead installation last year, will this time hold a Justice exhibit titled Blinded By The Lights.

The rest of the poster runs wide. Phoebe Bridgers, Weezer, Robyn, Zara Larsson, Steve Lacy, Caroline Polachek, Four Tet, Peggy Gou, Kehlani, Giorgio Moroder, Underworld, Freddie Gibbs, Social Distortion, MUNA, Tove Lo, Shygirl, the Avalanches and the Damned all appear, alongside Magdalena Bay, Role Model, Mariah The Scientist, Remi Wolf, Drain Gang, American Football and Gang Of Youths.

Stereogum, which published the lineup, flagged a handful of bookings as particular surprises, among them Fetty Wap and Enigma. Pinegrove also turns up on the bill, the band's first announced festival appearance since going on hiatus in 2023.

Smaller-type names on the poster include underscores, Nettspend, xaviersobased, This Is Lorelei, Chanel Beads, Lambrini Girls, Mary In The Junkyard, Snow Strippers, Bassvictim, Boy Harsher, Basement, Dinner Party, Haute Freddy, Getdown Services, Twisted Teens, Adéla, Nirosta Steel, Florence Road, Tiffany Day, Angine de Poitrine, ear and Mike D 5D.

Ticket information is live on the Coachella website.

items.title: Usher and Chris Brown Cancel Two More Performances as Feud Reports Heat Up
items.summary:
Usher and Chris Brown have scrapped two more dates on their co-headlining R&B Tour, pushing the total number of canceled shows to six. The latest to go are a November 16 date at SoFi Stadium in Los Angeles and a December 6 show at Hard Rock Stadium in Miami, both now listed as canceled on Ticketmaster.

All six canceled concerts were added to the tour's schedule in August, after the original routing was set. Nine dates remain, with the run currently scheduled to finish in Tampa on December 12.

The cancellations arrive alongside unconfirmed reports of friction between the two headliners, including accounts of a loud backstage argument in Atlanta. Variety reported that representatives for both artists and for Live Nation, which is promoting the tour, did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

The November 5 show at Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta has become the focal point. That concert ran three hours late, drew complaints about sound quality and did not include the joint performance the pair had given on earlier dates. TMZ reported that the disagreement concerned the start time, with Brown pushing to hold the show for fans stuck in traffic, and that the two have not resolved the matter.

Earlier cancellations in Baltimore, Cincinnati, South Carolina and Indianapolis were attributed to the health and well-being of the touring party and crew. A statement from Lucas Oil Stadium in Indianapolis, cited by Ticket News, said "the demands of a tour of this length and scale are significant, and these adjustments will allow the tour to continue safely and sustainably through the remaining scheduled performances."

Brown's conduct has drawn scrutiny before, from his 2009 assault on Rihanna to a 2023 altercation at a London nightclub that resulted in a suspended sentence last month. Commercially, the tour has performed well regardless: Pollstar put its gross above $280 million through October 3.

items.title: Dua Lipa, Tame Impala and SZA to Headline Coachella 2027
items.summary:
Coachella has named Dua Lipa, Tame Impala and SZA as the headliners for its 2027 edition, with SZA teasing the announcement on social media ahead of the poster's release. The festival returns to the Empire Polo Club in Indio, California, across two weekends, April 9-11 and April 16-18.

Daddy Yankee takes the special slot that functions as a de facto fourth headliner, and Justice will debut an installation called Blinded by the Lights in the Bunker. Madonna is billed in the Dance Tent, a return to the same stage she played in 2006 around the release of Confessions on a Dance Floor.

The upper tiers of the poster also include Phoebe Bridgers, Don Toliver, Zara Larsson, Weezer, Dom Dolla, Kygo, Empire of the Sun and Role Model. Further down sit Kehlani, Jisoo, Tiesto, Adéla, Maneskin, Four Tet, Becky G, the Neighbourhood, Remi Wolf, Victoria Monét, Caroline Polachek, Underworld, Pinegrove, Leon Thomas, Peggy Gou, Giorgio Moroder, Mariah the Scientist, Babymonster, Magdalena Bay, Murda Beatz, Martin Garrix and others.

Passes go on sale November 13 at noon Pacific through the festival's website, according to Variety, with hotel packages bundling tickets, lodging and transportation available for both weekends. YouTube returns as the exclusive livestream partner for a fifteenth year.

The announcement follows a 2026 edition headlined by Sabrina Carpenter, Justin Bieber, Karol G and Anyma. Madonna appeared during Carpenter's second-weekend set to perform their single "Bring Your Love" for the first time.
